note.p: Ed Pope suggests as a possibility: Holdens directory 1811 John Saunders broker 3 Hand-court Upper Thames-st / John Cunningam Saunders surgeon, Ely-place. This may be the John Saunders that Godwin notes in December (7th) 1809). But the contacts start on 13 September 1796 with 'Call on Saunders , Clifford's Inn' and Clifford's Inn is a place where attorney's in Chancery had their offices and was used more widely for training and residence for the legal profession. Moreover, there are later references to a clerk from Saunders (14/6/1814) and connections to the lawyer Ballachey- which seem to support the view that this is someone in the law and with interests in inheritance arrangements! So we have coded Saunders to the lawyer, and have a separate entry for the Broker John Saunders. We do not believe that Miss Saunders is connected.
